title: refactor(gen): let providers reject bad parameters
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Gen no longer keeps its own copies of provider limits. The provider rejects bad values, and gen passes its error to the caller (`ensureUpstreamOk`, `toReplicateUpstreamError`).

- Removes aspect-ratio lists, size ranges and duration checks from the Seedance, Seedream, Gemini Omni, Wan, MiniMax H3, Azure MAI/FLUX and fal Qwen handlers
- Removes every per-model reference-image cap (Seedream, FLUX.2, FLUX.3, Gemini, Vertex, p-image-edit, Alibaba, InferencePort, Grok, fal Qwen, Azure MAI); MAI edits use the first image
- Removes the video frame-count check; extra frame images are ignored or rejected by the provider
- Removes audio text-length, voice-ID, voice and format checks (ElevenLabs, Stable Audio, Fish, Grok TTS, Azure tts-1, DeepInfra)
- Removes resolution checks that `params.ts` already makes; Lightning Image Turbo now ignores the requested size (it only outputs 1024×1024)
- Keeps SFX mp3-only (billing) and checks for values a provider would ignore or change without an error (Azure 16/32px steps, CSM 200 chars, Gemini TTS, fixed fps/duration)

Tests for the removed rejections are deleted. tsc and biome are clean; the full gen suite passes (2526/2532, 6 skipped).

Fixes #16577

gist.headline: Let the provider decide
gist.blurb: Gen stops guessing what each model will accept. Image, video, and audio requests go to the provider for validation, and its error comes back with the answer.
gist.summary: Gen removes duplicated provider-specific limits for image, video, and audio parameters, passing rejected values through to providers and returning their errors while retaining checks for values providers would silently ignore or change.
gist.impact: Callers get provider-generated errors instead of Gen's potentially stale rejections; MAI edits use the first reference image, and Lightning Image Turbo remains fixed at 1024×1024 regardless of requested size.
